newsitem.title: UK: BT /MCI seen better placed for Asia.
newsitem.headline: BT /MCI seen better placed for Asia.

text.p: The $20 billion merger between British Telecommunications (BT) and MCI of the U.S. is likely to make the enlarged group a more viable partner to get a foothold in the lucrative Asia-Pacific markets, analysts said on Monday.

The combined group, with a market capitalisation of $54 billion according to last Thursday's share prices, will be called Concert Plc and will be the second largest international telephone company in the world.
"I think it does make them more plausible in Asia Pacific," said one analyst. "Those countries want to see who has the most clout and whose gang they are going to join."
"This clearly gives Concert greater clout," he added.
"This is one benefit (of the merger) rather than the benefit. In the shorter term, the real benefits come from accessing the local loop in the U.S. which is business, not residential," he added.
BT has had a technology agreement with Japan's state-owned Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp for about 10 years.

BT chief executive Sir Peter Bonfield told reporters on Sunday, after announcing the mega-merger with MCI, that he would soon be on the phone to NTT executives. Telecoms groups see phenonemal growth in Japanese international traffic.
One analyst noted that international traffic out of Japan was similar to that out of Hong Kong -- despite Japan's population, at about 124 million, being about 20 times that of Hong Kong.

"That gives an idea of what potential there might be to grow that market," he added. "The whole region is growing rapidly... and all telecoms groups are trying to do deals -- but Japan is the biggest prize."
But uncertainty still shrouds the Japanese telecoms market. The government has yet to decide how to regulate the market and whether or not to break NTT up into regional operators.
